column1: # The operand positions of loft's syntax — the slot register of the slot matrix (@PLN221).
# Columns, tab-separated: id, family, rule, count, runs, type, statement[, declaration].
#   rule    the formal rule that states how often this operand runs (`E-Left`, cited without
#           its `@FR-` sigil); `-` when no rule states it yet, which `check` lists as owed.
#   count   once | cond | step — exactly once; zero or one, decided by another operand; once
#   runs    how often the operand runs in THIS statement, in the prelude's world.
#   type    what the slot takes; a filler of that type goes in (scripts/syntax_fillers.tsv).
#   statement  one statement of `main` in scripts/syntax_slots_prelude.loft; `<S>` is the slot.
#   declaration  an optional top-level declaration the statement needs; `<S>` may sit there
#           instead, and then the declaration's parameters are the names a filler may use.
# A new operator, keyword or `#` attribute adds a row here, or a line in
# scripts/syntax_outside.tsv saying why it takes no operand: `slot_matrix.py check` fails
# until one of the two exists.
